# Open5e Pack Content Audit — Checklist & Roadmap

**Status:** measurement done, remediation not started.
**Numbers regenerated by:** `dart run tool/open5e_import/bin/audit_packs.dart`
(fields) and `dart run tool/open5e_import/bin/dupe_census.dart` (duplication).
**Measured:** 2026-07-30, against the 19 assets in `assets/open5e_packs/`.
**Gap-analysed:** 2026-07-30 — the roadmap was checked against the four outcomes
in §0.1 and found to cover only the first. Stages **U** (readers + wizard),
**M** (mechanics land), **T** (correctness + relational tooling) and **D**
(delivery) exist because of that pass; §2.5/§3.2 were corrected against measured
text divergence; and §3.5 records a shipped defect the field census could not
see — **396 of `open5e-tob3`'s 397 monsters have no actions**.

---

## 0. Start here

**This file is the single entry point for fixing official-pack content.** It is
self-contained: everything needed to pick up the work is below, and the links out
are optional depth, never prerequisites. Open a session with this file alone.

**The problem in two lines.** The bundled Open5e packs ship the right entities
with mostly empty fields — most sharply, 101 subclasses that attach to the correct
parent class and grant nothing. And **4,331 of their 20,712 entities (20.9%) are
copies of content the app already has in scope** — the built-in SRD pack ships it,
or another bundled pack does.

**Next action right now:** §6 phase **A0** — restore the source snapshot. It blocks
every other phase.

**Working loop.** Pick the topmost unchecked box in §6 → make the change in the
importer → `dart run tool/open5e_import/bin/build_packs.dart` → re-run both audit
tools → update the affected rows in §3/§5 and tick the box → `flutter analyze &&
flutter test` on the files you touched → update the affected `vault/` notes and
append a line to `vault/90-Meta/Vault-Changelog.md` (the SOP in `CLAUDE.md`
applies to importer changes like any other).
Keep every number in sync with the tools; never hand-edit one.

### 0.1 The four outcomes this file has to deliver

The phases exist to produce these four end states, not to turn cells green. Each
row names the phases that own it and the **gate that proves it** — if the gate
cannot be run, the outcome is not delivered no matter how many boxes are ticked.

| # | Outcome | Owning phases | Gate that proves it |
|:--:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Every official **and built-in** pack is processed correctly: entities present, fields populated **from the source** | A0–A2, B1–B8, V1, **T1–T3** | `verify_packs.dart` (T1) reports no field whose sampled value disagrees with the fixture; `audit_packs --builtin` (T2) has no unexplained ⚠; the relational gate (T3) is green — no actionless monster, no orphaned child row |
| 2 | Every field carrying a mechanic is tested and confirmed to work | B5, **M1–M3** | `bundled_pack_resolve_test` covers **all 19 packs** and asserts one resolved sheet value per mechanic field each pack writes; what stays non-mechanical is declared (M3) |
| 3 | Packs link instead of duplicating; no duplicate content, no redundant fields | **L0**, L1–L3 | `dupe_census` (fidelity-fixed) shows no unexplained redundancy, section C's "nothing installed" is 0 under **runtime-identical matching**, and `requires` is non-empty for every linker |
| 4 | Character creation works with every pack | **U1, U2** | a wizard-level test per pack family builds a committable draft, and every `_ref` field the wizard filters on is read through `resolveEntityRef` |
| — | The work reaches users | **D1, D2** | `pack_version` bumped, catalog rebuilt, `publish_catalog` uploads instead of skipping, installed packs upgrade |

Outcome 1 was the doc's original subject. Outcomes 2–4 were **assumed** by the
original roadmap and are why Stages M, U, T and D exist: filling a field proves
nothing about its value (T), about it reaching a sheet (M), about it reaching the
wizard (U), or about it reaching a user (D).

### Scope — everything, from scratch

**In scope:** the 19 bundled Open5e packs in `assets/open5e_packs/` and the offline
importer that produces them — **all of it, including content that already ships and
fields that already measure 100%.** This is a from-scratch pass, not a gap-filling
pass. Concretely:

- A ✅ row is a **claim to re-verify**, not a result to trust. `audit_packs.dart`
  counts values, not correctness; the ⚠ marker exists because several categories
  were found "100% filled" with a hardcoded constant. Every green row gets checked
  against the source at least once before this audit closes (§6 V1).
- Every card that already ships is re-examined for the question §2 asks: *should
  this entity exist at all, or is it a copy of something already in scope?*
- Every ⛔/⚪ policy row is re-derived rather than inherited. Several of them
  ("no base items ship in item packs", "a class `_ref` would dangle") were written
  before package links existed and are **no longer true** — see §2.4.

**The built-in SRD 5.2.1 pack** (`lib/domain/entities/schema/builtin/srd_core/`)
is in scope as the **link target** and, since the 2026-07-30 gap pass, in scope to
**measure** (§6 T2) — out of scope only as an *edit* target. It has its own tests
(`feature_grant_edge_test`, `grant_contract_test`) and its own version counter
(`srdCorePackVersion`), but it has **no field census**: `audit_packs.dart` reads
`assets/open5e_packs` only, so nothing today would notice a ⚠ constant or an
empty required field in the 21 k lines of `srd_core/`. Every softRef this audit
writes lands there, so a hole in it is a hole in every pack. Measure it, report
it, fix it in a separate change with its own `srdCorePackVersion` bump.

**Character creation is an outcome, not a side effect.** The wizard is in scope
(§6 Stage U): a pack whose fields are perfectly filled still fails outcome 4 if a
step's filter cannot read the shape the importer writes. That is not hypothetical
— see §2.3.1.

**Optional depth:** `open5e_import_roadmap.md` (how the importer was originally
built, licensing, phases P0–P6). Read it only if the map above is not enough —
parts of it are superseded by this file and marked as such.

### The target architecture — read before writing a mapper fix

Every fix in §6 obeys two contracts. The first (§2) is new and takes precedence
when they interact: **never create what you can link.** The second is the
**named-field grant system** that replaced the effect DSL on 2026-07-28.
`vault/20-Systems/Grant-Resolution.md` is the authority on it;
`CharacterResolver.grantFieldKeys` is the closed 41-key contract. Four rules
constrain what a correct fix looks like:

1. **One mechanic, one field.** There is no `kind`/`predicate`/`scales_with` row
   language any more — `FieldType.featEffectList` and `grantedModifiers` are
   deleted. Never invent a key; if a mechanic has no field, that is a schema
   change with four guards to satisfy (`grant_contract_test`,
   `grant_field_isolation_test`), not an importer change.
2. **Class, Subclass and Background deliberately do NOT carry the grant block.**
   Seeing `subclass` at 1-of-8 filled and "fixing" it by handing it the block
   would recreate exactly the two-fields-one-mechanic ambiguity the removal was
   for — and `grant_contract_test` fails on it. Their grants go in their own
   typed fields (`saving_throw_refs`, `armor_training_refs`, `granted_skill_refs`,
   …), and everything level-gated goes on a `features` row.
3. **Level-gated mechanics live on a Feat card, referenced from the `features`
   row** — `{level, name, description, granted_feat_refs, granted_trait_refs, …}`.
   The class card names *which* feat arrives at *which* level; the Feat card
   carries the mechanics via the grant block. This is the forward edge that
   replaced `feat.auto_granted_by`. Scaling is a `{lvl: value}` table
   (`extra_attack_count_by_level`), never a formula.
4. **Nothing is silently dropped.** Rules the engine cannot pre-compute
   (advantage, rerolls, roll-time riders, timing) belong in `mechanical_notes`,
   one rule per line — they render on the sheet under "Other Effects". Today
   `mechanical_notes` is **0% across every bundled category**, which means every
   §5 row below reading "stays in prose" is currently invisible to the player.
   Routing them there is the cheapest real win in this audit (§6 B5).

## 1. Why this exists

Five distinct gaps, with five distinct fixes. Do not conflate them. Gaps 1–3 are
about the **assets**; gaps 4–5 are about everything between a correct asset and a
player seeing it, and were added by the 2026-07-30 gap analysis.

**Gap 1 — empty fields.** The bundled packs ship the right **entities** but mostly
empty **fields**. A player installing *Tome of Heroes* gets 76 subclasses that
attach to the correct parent class and then grant nothing — they carry
`description` and `parent_class_ref` and not one other field. → §5, phases B1–B7.

**Gap 2 — duplicated entities.** 20.9% of the bundled corpus shares a
`(slug, name)` key with content already in scope: 1,660 keys the built-in SRD pack
ships, and 3,393 copies of names appearing in more than one bundled pack. Since
2026-07-29 a package can **link** another instead of copying it, so the genuine
duplicates are deletions, not merges. **But most of that 20.9% is not duplication
at all** — 85% of it is `trait`/`creature-action` rows owned by a single statblock,
90% of which say different things (§2.5). Read the number as a collision surface
and let the policy table, not the total, drive the work. → §2, §3.2, phases L0–L2.

**Gap 3 — refs written as prose.** Where a card *should* point at another card, the
importer mostly writes English instead. `feat.prereq_class_refs` is 0% because the
prerequisite class is named in the description text; `spell.class_refs` is 0%
because of a policy note that package links have now invalidated. Only **135**
cross-package refs exist in the entire 20,712-entity corpus. → §2.3, and a gate on
every B phase.

**Gap 4 — readers that cannot see a correct ref.** The sheet resolves every
envelope shape; **the wizard does not**. Four chargen call sites read
`spell.class_refs` as a raw `List<String>` of ids and match with `.contains()`, so
the softRef Map that §2.3 tells you to write matches *nothing* there — and today's
packaged spells are visible only through a `tags` fallback that the same fix would
retire. Filling a field is therefore not the last step; §2.3.1 and Stage U are. →
outcome 4.

**Gap 5 — nothing published.** `emit.dart` hardcodes `pack_version: '1.0.0'`,
`build_catalog` derives the immutable `r2_path` from that version, and
`publish_catalog` **skips** an object that already exists unless `--force`. Every
pack is `1.0.0` and already uploaded, so a perfect rebuild changes nothing for any
user, and no installed pack has an upgrade trigger. → Stage D.

The wiring for what does exist is not the problem. All 97 `parent_class_ref`
softRefs on the bundled subclasses resolve by name against the built-in SRD classes
(Cleric ×11, Wizard ×11, Monk ×9, …, zero misses). That is the model the rest of
this work copies.

### Cause codes

Every row below carries one. They are not interchangeable — `S` is upstream work,
`L`/`M`/`D` are ours, `P`/`N` are closed.

| Code | Meaning | Where the fix lands |
|:--:|---|---|
| `S` | Not in the source dump for the documents we ship | re-fetch, or accept as permanent |
| `L` | In the dump, in a fixture file the importer never **loads** | `bin/build_packs.dart` + `sources.dart` |
| `M` | File loaded, field not **mapped** or mapped wrong | `mappers/*.dart` |
| `D` | **Duplicate / should be a link** — the value exists, but it points at (or *is*) a copy of content already in scope | `mappers/*.dart` + `metadata.links` |
| `P` | Deliberately not mapped, decision on record | none — link the decision |
| `N` | App field has no Open5e counterpart | none — permanently empty |

### Status markers

| | Meaning |
|:--:|---|
| ✅ | Every entity carries it — **still to be re-verified (§6 V1)** |
| 🟡 | Some do — the gap is the finding |
| 🔴 | Never written |
| ⚠ | Filled, but with the **same constant on every row** — the mapper wrote a default instead of reading the source. A 100% column with ⚠ is not coverage. |
| 🔗 | Should resolve to existing content instead of being re-created or left in prose |
| ⛔ | Policy: intentionally empty |
| ⚪ | No source field exists |

## 2. The linking contract — never create what you can link

**This is the most important rule in this document, and it outranks every fill
target in §5.** A row that reaches 100% by minting duplicate cards is a
regression, not a fix.

Package links landed on 2026-07-29 (`vault/20-Systems/Package-Links.md`). A package
can now **link** another package: the two stores stay separate, nothing is copied,
and the linked package's entities become visible inside the linking package and
follow it into every world import, catalog download and character build. That
mechanism is finished and tested. This audit is the content work it unblocked.

### 2.1 The built-in pack is already in scope everywhere — do not re-ship it

Every bundled pack effectively links the built-in SRD 5.2.1 pack already, through
three independent paths, none of which needs a declaration:

| Context | Why built-in content is in scope |
|---|---|
| Package editor | `packageReferenceOverlayProvider(name)` = built-in SRD entities ∪ the closure's entities, injected read-only by `EntityNotifier(referenceOverlayFor:)` |
| World | `SrdCoreBootstrap.ensureImported` links `SRD 5.2.1 Core` into every D&D-5e-v2 world at creation, and self-heals a world missing the link |
| Character creation / resolve | `mergeBuiltinWithPackages` starts from the built-in map and layers packages on top; `layerCharacterPackages` does the same on the card side |

**Consequence:** a bundled pack that ships its own "Acolyte" — the *same* Acolyte —
is not adding content. It is shadowing content that is already there, and it costs
the user a duplicate row in every picker. Those entities should simply not be
emitted.

**The consequence is about identical content, not identical names.** §2.5 measures
how often those two come apart: a pack's "Fireball" may be an A5E restat, and its
"Amphibious" is usually a per-creature sentence that only *looks* like the built-in
row. Establish which one you are holding before deleting anything.

An explicit `metadata.links` entry pointing at the built-in pack is therefore
**unnecessary** — and would be wrong in the catalog, which has no entry for a
built-in pack.

### 2.2 Pack→pack links need a declaration — and it needs both keys

For the 3,393 copies shared *between* bundled packs, one pack keeps the content and
the others link it. That link is declared in the pack payload:

```jsonc
// in a *.pkg.json, alongside title / license / pack_version
"metadata": {
  "links": [ { "slug": "open5e-toh", "name": "Tome of Heroes" } ]
}
```

**Both keys are required, and they hold different strings.** This is the sharp edge
of the whole phase:

- `slug` — the **catalog slug**, i.e. the target's `package_name`
  (`open5e-toh`). `build_catalog._requiredSlugs` reads `slug ?? package_id ?? name`
  and emits it as the catalog entry's `requires`, which `FirstPartyInstallNotifier`
  resolves transitively before installing. A link carrying only `name` produces a
  `requires` entry matching no manifest slug — silently skipped at install.
- `name` — the **installed local package name**, which is the target's
  `metadata.title` (`Tome of Heroes`), because `PackagePayloadImporter` names the
  local row after the title and falls back to the slug only when there is none.
  `PackageLink.fromJson` reads `package_id`/`packageId` and `name`/`package_name`
  and **ignores `slug` entirely**, so a link carrying only `slug` resolves to
  nothing in the app.

All 19 titles are currently unique, so name resolution is unambiguous.
`PackageLinkService` resolves `package_id` first and falls back to `name`; leave
`package_id` out of a built payload, since the local row id is minted at install.

Today **every pack emits `requires: []`** — the wiring exists end to end and has no
data flowing through it.

### 2.3 Links inside cards — the part that is easy to get wrong

Dropping duplicate *entities* is only half of it. The other half is that **every
reference a card makes must resolve to existing content, not create a new copy of
it and not sit in prose.** This applies to every field in §5 that ends in `_ref`
or `_refs`, and it is the main way a B phase can quietly make things worse.

The worked example: an official pack's feat has "Prerequisite: Paladin" in its
description. There are three ways to "fix" `prereq_class_refs`, and two are wrong.

| | What it does | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Mint a `class` card named "Paladin" in the pack and hard-`ref` it | adds a 3rd Paladin to the user's picker; the character's actual Paladin levels are on the *built-in* Paladin, so the gate silently never matches | ❌ never |
| Leave it in the description | prerequisite is invisible to the wizard's gating; the field stays 0% | ❌ that is the current state |
| `softRef('class', 'Paladin')` | `resolveEntityRef` → `findEntityIdByName` lands on whichever Paladin is in scope — the built-in one — at resolve time | ✅ |

Resolution order for **any** ref the importer emits:

1. Tier-0 vocabulary (ability, skill, damage type, condition, size, sense, …) →
   `lookup()` → `{_lookup, name}`, resolved to the campaign's Tier-0 uuid at import.
   Unchanged by any of this.
2. Target exists in the **built-in pack** → `softRef(slug, name)`, and **do not
   emit a local copy of that entity**.
3. Target exists in **another bundled pack** → `softRef(slug, name)` **and** add
   that pack to `metadata.links` (§2.2). A softRef alone still resolves in a world
   where both packs happen to be installed, but the link is what makes that
   happen on purpose.
4. Target ships in **this pack and nowhere upstream** → hard `ref()`, resolved by
   the two-pass refgraph, build-gated against dangling.
5. Nothing to point at → drop the ref and write the rule into `mechanical_notes`
   (§0 rule 4) plus a line in `unmapped_report.json`. Never invent a card.

Three facts about how a softRef lands, all of which matter when deciding:

- `findEntityIdByName` matches on `(categorySlug, name)` and is **case
  sensitive** — the index key is the raw `"$slug $name"`. `"thieves' tools"` does
  not find `"Thieves' Tools"`. The census lowercases (§3.4), so it will tell you
  such a ref resolves when the app drops it.
- It is **qualifier tolerant**: `"Magic Initiate (Cleric)"` falls back to
  `"Magic Initiate"`. This cuts both ways — the built-in pack ships *both*
  `Amphibious` and `Amphibious (Dragon)`, so a softRef to
  `"Amphibious (Aboleth)"` silently lands on the generic row and puts the wrong
  text on the sheet. Qualifier tolerance is a fallback, never a naming strategy:
  emit the name the target actually ships.
- Its index is **first-writer-wins over map iteration order**. With duplicates in
  play, *which* "Fireball" a ref resolves to is an accident of merge order. That is
  the second reason to delete duplicates rather than tolerate them: they make ref
  resolution nondeterministic in a way no test asserts.

The census tracks this surface directly (§3.2 C). It is currently 135 refs —
106 to the built-in pack, 29 that could be in-pack hard refs, 0 dangling, and
**0 to another bundled pack**.

### 2.3.1 A correct ref is not a visible ref — check the reader first

`CharacterResolver` accepts all three envelopes everywhere (`_readRefList` →
`_resolveRef` → `resolveEntityRef`), which is why §2.3 works *on the sheet*. The
chargen UI is not uniformly on that path, and a `_ref` field it filters on is
therefore a **two-sided change**: importer *and* reader.

The live case is `spell.class_refs` (§5.6, phases L3/B7). Four call sites read it
as a list of plain id strings:

| Call site | What it drives |
|---|---|
| `wizard/steps/spells_step.dart` `_classRefs` | the cantrip / prepared-spell picker |
| `wizard/character_creation_wizard_screen.dart` (`spellCount`) | **whether the spells step is required at all** — 0 matches means the step is skipped |
| `wizard/steps/feats_step.dart` | Magic Initiate–style feat spell lists at creation |
| `pending_choice_resolver_dialog.dart` (×2) | the same lists at level-up |

Each does `(fields['class_refs'] as List).contains(classId)`; a `{slug, name}`
Map matches nothing, and `whereType<String>()` drops it outright. Packaged spells
reach these lists today **only** through the parallel `tags` fallback (the class
name as a bare tag, recovered from the v1 fixtures — §4 A0). So:

> Writing `spell.class_refs` as softRefs and retiring the `tags` route in the same
> change **removes every bundled spell from character creation** while every
> number in §3 and §5 improves. This is the shape of regression this audit is most
> likely to ship.

Rule: before filling any `*_ref`/`*_refs` field, grep for its readers. If a reader
is not on `resolveEntityRef`, put it on `resolveEntityRef` **first** (Stage U1),
keep the old route alive until the new one is proven, and only then retire it.

### 2.4 Policy rows that package links have invalidated

These were correct when written and are not any more. Each is re-opened in §5:

| Row | Old rationale | Why it no longer holds |
|---|---|---|
| `spell.class_refs` (required, 0%) | "spell packs ship no class entities, so a `_ref` would dangle" | a softRef to a built-in class does not dangle — it is exactly what 97 subclasses already do |
| `magic-item.base_item_ref` (0%) | "no base items ship in item packs" | the built-in pack ships weapons, armor and gear; softRef by name |
| `background.default_inventory_refs` / `class.default_inventory_refs` | superseded by `equipment_choice_groups`, backed by 159 synthesised gear stubs | link built-in gear instead of synthesising stubs (§6 B6) |
| `monster.gear_refs`, `monster.spell_refs` | ⚪ no counterpart | the *targets* now exist and resolve; whether the source names them is a separate `S` question to re-check |

### 2.5 A name collision is not proof the content is identical — measured

The census matches on `(category slug, lowercased name)`, so every row it reports
is a name collision the resolver can really face. It is **not** evidence that the
two cards say the same thing, and the 2026-07-30 pass measured exactly how weak
the evidence is.

**Measurement (reproduce with the snippet in §7):** of the 1,937 cross-pack shared
names in `creature-action` + `trait`, **1,749 (90.3%) carry different description
text**:

| Category | Shared names | …with differing text | Redundant copies | Distinct variants |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `creature-action` | 1,264 | 1,201 (95%) | 1,679 | 1,598 |
| `trait` | 673 | 548 (81%) | 1,105 | 949 |

The examples the previous revision of this section called safe boilerplate are the
worst offenders, because the text names its creature:

| Name | Copies | Distinct texts |
|---|--:|--:|
| `creature-action` "Multiattack" | 8 | **8** |
| `trait` "Pack Tactics" | 7 | **7** |
| `trait` "Amphibious" | 7 | **5** — "The aboleth can breathe air and water" vs "The dragon…" vs "Can breathe air and water." |
| `trait` "Magic Resistance" | 7 | 6 |
| `trait` "Keen Smell" | 6 | 5 |
| `creature-action` "Move" | 6 | 6 |

**And these are not library entities.** A monster hard-`_ref`s its own children:
`action_refs`, `trait_refs`, `reaction_refs`, `legendary_action_refs` are uuid
lists pointing at rows that exist for that one statblock. Collapsing them by name
does not deduplicate a shared card — it reassigns another creature's text to this
creature. The built-in pack already concedes the point by shipping
`Amphibious (Dragon)` next to `Amphibious`.

> **Policy: `creature-action` and `trait` rows owned by a monster are out of scope
> for L1/L2 dedup.** They are per-statblock children, not shareable content. The
> only defensible dedup there is *byte-identical text within one publisher's
> corpus*, and it buys little. Route them through a `--text` census column (L0)
> and leave them alone otherwise.

**What that does to the headline number.** 3,676 of the 4,331 redundant entities
(85%) are `trait` + `creature-action`. Excluding them, and applying the keep
policies below, the genuinely actionable set is roughly:

| Category | Actionable | Why |
|---|--:|---|
| `adventuring-gear` | 47 | synthesised stubs, no description/cost/weight — drop unconditionally (§6 B6) |
| `monster` | 997 → **per document** | ToB 2016 vs ToB 2023 are deliberate separate editions; A5E restats. Only same-edition reprints drop |
| `spell` | 318 → **~5** | 313 are A5E restats (keep) |
| `background` | 13 | 12 are A5E (keep unless the restat is cosmetic) + 1 cross-pack |
| `feat`, `magic-item` | 2 | inspect individually |

So "20.9% redundant" is the **collision surface**, not the work item. The work
item after policy is a few hundred entities, dominated by the gear stubs. §6 L1/L2
exit criteria are written against that, not against driving section A to 0.

Two documents where dropping the bundled copy would destroy real content:

- **Level Up: Advanced 5e** (`open5e-a5e-*`, `game_system: a5e`) deliberately
  restats 5e material. Its "Fireball" is not the SRD "Fireball", and 313 of
  *Adventurer's Guide*'s 371 spells collide by name with the built-in pack. A5E is
  the case where the answer is most likely **keep**.
- **Tome of Beasts (2016) vs Tome of Beasts 1 (2023 Edition)** are two editions of
  the same book, shipped as two packs on purpose.

`game_system` (`5e-2014` / `a5e`) is display-only metadata — nothing in the app
filters on it, so it cannot carry the decision automatically. The decision is
per-document policy, made once and recorded in §6 L1/L2, not per-row guesswork:

- monster-owned `trait` / `creature-action` rows → **keep** (above);
- synthesised `adventuring-gear` stubs → drop unconditionally (§6 B6 — they carry
  no description, no cost and no weight, and include parse artifacts such as
  "pet monkey wearing a tiny fez");
- statblocks and spells → per document, and A5E most likely keeps its own.

### 3.3 Catalog state

`assets/first_party/manifest.json` carries 19 package entries, **all with
`requires: []`** and **all at `version: 1.0.0`**. Its `counts` and `size_bytes`
also carry pre-existing drift from a pack regeneration that never rebuilt the
manifest — so the manifest is stale independently of anything here, and A0's
rebuild diff must account for it.

The version is not cosmetic. The delivery chain is:

`emit.dart` `pack_version: '1.0.0'` (hardcoded) → `build_catalog` `version` →
`r2_path = package/<slug>@<version>.json.gz` (documented as **immutable**) →
`publish_catalog` `_exists()` → **skip unless `--force`** → client installs
`entry.version` and stamps it as `metadata.catalog_version`.

Consequences this audit has to plan for (§6 Stage D):

- Re-running the whole roadmap and republishing uploads **nothing**: every object
  already exists at `@1.0.0`.
- `--force` overwriting a versioned path contradicts the immutability contract and
  leaves clients with no signal that anything changed.
- There is no installed-pack upgrade path at all: `FirstPartyInstallNotifier`
  installs, it never diffs a stored `catalog_version` against the manifest.
- In debug, `BundledPacksBootstrap` sidesteps all of this with a content hash
  (`metadata.bundled_content_hash`) — which is exactly why the problem is easy to
  miss while developing. Release builds do not ship the assets at all.

### 3.4 What the tools do **not** prove

Every phase in §6 inherits these limits; three of them are why Stages T, M and U
exist. Fixing the tools is cheaper than re-doing a phase that passed a bad gate.

| Claim you might read into a green number | Why it does not follow | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| "`audit_packs` says 100%, so the field is right" | It counts *presence*. `0`/`false`/a constant all count; the ⚠ marker only catches a value identical on **every** row of a category | **T1** |
| "The bundled packs are audited, so the content is audited" | `audit_packs` and `dupe_census` read `assets/open5e_packs` only. The built-in pack — the target of every softRef — is never measured | **T2** |
| "Section C says 0 dangling, so every ref lands" | `dupe_census._key` **lowercases** the name; `findEntityIdByName` is **case sensitive** and additionally strips a trailing parenthetical. The census is looser in one direction and stricter in the other, so it can report a resolved ref the app drops, and a dangling ref the app resolves | **L0** |
| "A `(slug, name)` collision means duplicated content" | 90.3% of cross-pack collisions in the two biggest categories have different text (§2.5) | **L0** |
| "The field is filled and the resolver reads it, so it works" | The wizard has its own readers, several of which take raw ids only (§2.3.1) | **U1** |
| "`bundled_pack_resolve_test` is green, so the packs resolve" | It covers **3 of 19** packs (`toh`, `a5e-ag`, `open5e`) with ~6 assertions, all about the three assets `migrate_pack_assets.dart` rewrote | **M1** |
| "Every `monster` field is 88% filled, so the statblocks are fine" | The census is **per field, per category** — it cannot see that a specific pack's monsters have no actions, or that a relationship landed in the wrong bucket. §3.5 found exactly that | **T3** |
| "The assets are correct, so users have correct content" | Nothing is published; see §3.3 | **D1** |

### 3.5 Relational completeness — the census's blind spot (measured 2026-07-30)

`audit_packs.dart` answers *"do some entities carry this field?"*. It cannot
answer *"does every monster have actions?"*, and the difference is a shipped
defect that the ✅-heavy `monster` table hid.

**400 of 2,885 bundled monsters (13.9%) have an empty `action_refs`** — and 396 of
them are in one pack:

| Pack | Monsters | With no `action_refs` |
|---|--:|--:|
| `open5e-tob3` | 397 | **396 (99.7%)** |
| `open5e-a5e-mm` | 586 | 3 |
| `open5e-tob2` | 383 | 1 |
| every other pack | — | 0 |

The rows are not missing — they are in the **wrong bucket**. `mapCreatures`
switches on `CreatureAction.action_type` and defaults to `action_refs`; in
`tob3` almost nothing hits the default:

| Pack | `action_refs` | `bonus_action_refs` | `reaction_refs` | `legendary_action_refs` |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `open5e-tob` | 1,305 | 0 | 37 | 85 |
| `open5e-tob2` | 1,215 | 0 | 41 | 29 |
| `open5e-tob-2023` | 1,468 | 149 | 61 | 100 |
| `open5e-a5e-mm` | 1,867 | 265 | 174 | 230 |
| **`open5e-tob3`** | **2** | **136** | **96** | **75** |

So *Tome of Beasts 3* ships 397 statblocks whose attacks render as bonus actions,
reactions and legendary actions, with the Actions block empty. Cause is upstream
`action_type` values the mapper takes at face value, or a mis-set enum in that
document's fixtures — confirm against the restored snapshot (A0) and fix in **B8**.
Nothing in the audit, the build gate (no ref dangles — they all resolve, just into
the wrong list) or the tests would have caught it, which is why **T3** adds
relational assertions.

For contrast, the in-pack child model is otherwise sound: `_ensureChild` dedupes
children **by content hash** and disambiguates a colliding name with the creature
name ("Scimitar (Firetamer)"), so 905 rows are legitimately shared by several
monsters *because the text is identical*, and no row is orphaned (0 unreferenced
`creature-action` rows in every pack). That is the discipline any cross-pack dedup
(L1/L2) would have to match — hash, not name — and a further reason §2.5 keeps
these categories out of it: the app resolves a softRef **by name**, so a
deliberately qualified child name is exactly what qualifier-stripping
mis-resolves (§2.3).

## 4. Stage A — source snapshot

### A0. The snapshot is not on this machine — blocking

`open5e-api-staging/` is gitignored and absent. `build_packs.dart` defaults
`--data` to `../open5e-api-staging/data` (i.e. `<repo-root>/open5e-api-staging/`,
one level above `flutter_app/`). **Nothing in Stage B, and no pack rebuild for a
Stage L deletion, can happen until it is restored.**

The fixtures are the `data/` directory of the Open5e API repo's `staging` branch —
that branch name is where the `-staging` suffix comes from:

```sh
cd /path/to/dungeon-master-tool          # repo root, NOT flutter_app
git clone --branch staging --depth 1 \
    https://github.com/open5e/open5e-api.git open5e-api-staging
git -C open5e-api-staging rev-parse HEAD  # ← record this in the table below
ls open5e-api-staging/data/v2            # → en-publishing green-ronin kobold-press
                                         #   open5e somanyrobots wizards-of-the-coast
ls open5e-api-staging/data/v1            # ← NOT optional, see below
```

`open5e-api-staging/` is already in `.gitignore`, so it will not be committed.

> **`data/v1` is a hard dependency, not legacy.** The v2 fixtures leave
> `Spell.classes` empty for most third-party documents, so `build_packs.dart`
> builds a `spellNameLower → dnd_class` index from `data/v1/<doc>/Spell.json`
> (`_v1ClassIndex`, `_v1DocForV2`, `_v1GlobalPref`) and writes the result into the
> spell's **`tags`**. That tag list is the only thing making bundled spells
> visible in character creation today (§2.3.1). A snapshot without `v1`, or a
> `_v1DocForV2` entry missing for a newly added document, silently produces spells
> with no class linkage at all — and neither audit tool reports it, because `tags`
> is not a declared field. Add a spell-tag coverage line to the A0 diff review.

**Pin the snapshot in this file.** The default `--rev staging-2026-05-31` is a
label, not a commit, and upstream `staging` moves. Until the SHA is recorded here
no two runs of this audit are comparable:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Snapshot commit (`rev-parse HEAD`) | _(record on clone)_ |
| Cloned on | _(date)_ |
| `--rev` passed to `build_packs` | _(same SHA — do not leave the default)_ |

- [ ] Clone as above and fill the table
- [ ] Confirm `data/v1` is present and every document in `_v1DocForV2` resolves
- [ ] Rebuild and diff against the shipped assets — every difference is a finding,
      and the diff is expected to be non-empty (below)
- [ ] Spot-check spell `tags` coverage before/after the rebuild (guards the v1 path)
- [ ] Rebuild `assets/open5e_packs/manifest.json` and
      `assets/first_party/manifest.json`, and treat the resulting `counts` /
      `size_bytes` churn as the pre-existing drift it is (§3.3), not as a new change

> Two known reasons the rebuild will **not** be byte-identical:
> 1. **The shipped assets lag the mapper.** `mapSpecies` writes `granted_senses` as
>    `[{sense_ref: …}]`, but every shipped payload holds a bare
>    `[{_lookup: sense, name: Darkvision}]`. The delta is a free list of fixes that
>    were made but never rebuilt.
> 2. `tool/migrate_pack_assets.dart` rewrites assets in place, so part of what ships
>    was never produced by `build_packs` in the first place.
>
> Exit criterion is therefore *"every diff hunk is explained"*, not *"no diff"*.

### 5.2 `subclass` — 101 entities

The worst row in the audit: **1 of 8** declared fields ever written. Also the one
category whose single filled field is the **model for §2.3** — copy its pattern.

|:--:|---|---|:--:|--:|:--:|---|
| ✅🔗 | `parent_class_ref` | Identity | **yes** | 100% | | `subclass_of`; 97 softRefs verified to resolve against built-in classes, 4 in-pack hard refs |

> **`granted_at_level` changes wizard behaviour the moment it is filled.**
> `subclass_step.dart` `_grantedAtLevel` defaults a missing value to **1**, so all
> 101 bundled subclasses are currently pickable at level 1. Filling it correctly
> will lock most of them until level 3, clear a stale `draft.subclassId` through
> the post-frame `setSubclass(null)`, and change which subclasses the level-gate
> banner reports. That is the *correct* behaviour, but it is a user-visible change
> with no test today — B1 must land it together with a wizard-level assertion
> (Stage U2), not silently.

### 5.3 `species` (11) / `subspecies` (30)

`mapSpecies` matches trait rows by **name** (`'size'`, `'speed'`, `'darkvision'`,
`'languages'`, `'ability score increase'`). Open5e ships a `type` field on every trait
(`MODIFICATION_TYPES`: `ability_score`, `skill_proficiency`, `tool_proficiency`,
`language`, `equipment`, `feature`, `feat`, …). Switching to `type` is the single fix
behind most of these rows.

| | Field | Group | Req | species | subspecies | Cause | Source |
|:--:|---|---|:--:|--:|--:|:--:|---|
| 🟡 | `size_ref` | Identity | **yes** (species) | 63% | 33% | `M` | `SpeciesTrait` "Size" — name match misses variants |
| ✅⚠ | `creature_type_ref` | Identity | **yes** | 100% | 100% | `M`/⚪ | hardcoded `Humanoid` on all 41 — defensible default, but not sourced |
| 🔴 | `age` | Identity | | 0% | 0% | `M` | "Age" trait row |

### 5.7 The shared grant block

`_FB.grantBlock` puts the same 41 keys — `CharacterResolver.grantFieldKeys`, the
closed contract — on `feat`, `species`, `subspecies`, `magic-item` and `trait`.
`applyGrantsFrom` is the single reader, so one shared helper in the importer
covers all five card types; do not fix this per category.

**`class`, `subclass` and `background` are not on that list, by design.** They use
their own typed fields, and anything level-gated goes on a `features` row pointing
at a Feat card (§0 rule 3). Adding the block to them fails `grant_contract_test`.

Across every bundled pack, exactly **seven** of the 41 keys are ever written:
`granted_skill_proficiencies`, `granted_languages`, `ability_bonuses`,
`granted_damage_resistances`, `granted_senses` (species/subspecies), plus
`granted_armor_proficiencies`, `speed_bonus_ft` and `player_choices` on a handful
of feats. The other 34 are 🔴 everywhere.

Every `*_ref`/`*_refs` key in the block is a §2.3 site: its target is almost always
built-in content.

Highest value first:

1. **`mechanical_notes`** — 0% on all 6,423 traits and all 73 feats. Everything the
   §5 tables describe as "stays in prose" is meant to land here, one rule per
   line, and render under "Other Effects". Nothing else in this list makes a
   previously invisible rule visible.
2. `granted_senses` — needs `range_ft` parsed out of the trait text.
3. `granted_tool_proficiencies`, `granted_feat_refs` — both have a
   `MODIFICATION_TYPES` source tag that the mapper never reads; both 🔗.
4. `resource_pool_grants`, `extra_attack_count_by_level` — these are `{lvl: value}`
   tables, not formulas; they only become fillable after B1/B2 land the level data.

---

## 6. Roadmap

Ordered by leverage. Each phase has an exit criterion an audit tool can check.

**Every phase inherits three gates:**

1. **§2.3 ref gate** — it may not increase `dupe_census.dart`'s "nothing
   installed" count, and any `_ref` it writes must resolve to existing content.
   *(Trustworthy only once **L0** makes the census match the runtime — §3.4.)*
2. **§2.3.1 reader gate** — for every `_ref` field it fills, the readers of that
   field are on `resolveEntityRef`, or the phase does not ship.
3. **Repo gate** — `flutter analyze && flutter test` on the touched area, the
   affected `vault/` notes updated, and a `Vault-Changelog` line appended.

**Five phases need no source snapshot and can start today:** L0, U1, T2, T3, M1.
Everything else waits on A0.

### Stage A — unblock

- [ ] **A0 — Restore the source snapshot.**
      *Exit: `build_packs.dart` runs, and every hunk of the diff against the
      shipped assets is explained (§4 A0) — not "no diff".*
- [ ] **A1 — Fill the fixture matrix (§4 A1).** Every "never loaded" file gets a
      decision: load it, or record why not. Take `CrossReference.json` first — it
      may hand us the refs §2.3 currently name-matches.
      *Exit: no `[ ] decide` rows left in §4 A1.*

### Stage L — stop duplicating (unblocked by package links)

- [ ] **L0 — Make the census tell the truth.** *(no snapshot needed — do this
      first, every other L/B exit criterion depends on it.)* Three fixes to
      `dupe_census.dart`:
      (a) **match like the runtime** — `findEntityIdByName` is case sensitive and
      strips a trailing parenthetical; the census lowercases and does neither, so
      it both over- and under-reports (§3.4). Reuse the real function or mirror it
      exactly, and report the delta between "name matches" and "the app would
      resolve it" as its own line.
      (b) **report text divergence** — add an `identical text` column to sections
      A and B, so a collision that is genuinely the same card is distinguishable
      from one that only shares a name (§2.5: today 90.3% do not).
      (c) **bucket monster-owned children separately** — `creature-action` /
      `trait` rows reachable only from one monster's `action_refs` / `trait_refs`
      are not dedup candidates; count them in their own line so the headline
      number stops overstating the work by ~4×.
      *Exit: the census prints an actionable-redundancy figure that §2.5's policy
      table explains row for row, and §1/§3.2 are rewritten against it.*
- [ ] **L1 — Drop what the built-in pack already ships.** Build a `(slug, name)`
      index of the built-in pack inside the importer (both
      `generateBuiltinDnd5eV2Schema().seedRows` and `buildSrdCorePack()` are pure
      Dart and already importable from `tool/` — `dupe_census.dart` does exactly
      this), and skip emitting a colliding entity — **after** a per-document
      keep/drop policy is recorded per §2.5 (A5E keeps its spells and backgrounds;
      monster-owned traits and actions are **not** candidates). Any ref that
      pointed at a dropped card becomes a `softRef` to the built-in one, emitted
      with the target's exact name (§2.3, case sensitivity).
      *Exit: every remaining section-A row is covered by a written keep policy in
      §2.5, section C's "nothing installed" is still 0 under L0 matching, and the
      dropped-entity count matches the policy table — not "section A is 0".*
- [ ] **L2 — One owner per shared name; the rest link.** For the shared names L0
      classifies as genuinely identical content, pick the owning pack, drop the
      copies, and declare `metadata.links` on the linkers with **both** the catalog
      `slug` and the local `name` (§2.2). The emitter is `emit.assemblePack`, which
      today writes a fixed `metadata` map with no `links` key at all — that is the
      code change, not a mapper edit.
      *Exit: a test round-trips a built pack's `metadata.links` through
      `PackageLink.fromJson` **and** `build_catalog._requiredSlugs` (both keys
      present, both resolve), `assets/first_party/manifest.json` shows non-empty
      `requires` on the packs that now link, and installing a linker from the
      catalog pulls its target (`FirstPartyInstallNotifier.install`).*
- [ ] **L3 — Turn existing prose into refs.** *(blocked by U1.)* The 🔗 rows in §5
      that already ship in some form: `subclass` parent tags, feat prerequisites,
      `spell.class_refs`, `magic-item.base_item_ref`.
      *Exit: `dupe_census.dart` section C grows, "nothing installed" stays 0 under
      L0 matching, `bundled_pack_resolve_test` proves one such ref reaching a
      sheet, and — for `spell.class_refs` — the wizard test from U2 proves the
      spell list is not empty **before** the `tags` route is retired.*

### Stage U — make the wizard see it (outcome 4)

- [ ] **U1 — Put every chargen ref reader on `resolveEntityRef`.** *(no snapshot
      needed.)* The five call sites in §2.3.1 plus any other chargen filter that
      does `(fields[x] as List).contains(id)`. Keep the `tags` fallback in place;
      this phase only *adds* the ability to see a softRef.
      *Exit: no chargen filter matches ids by raw `String` equality against a
      `*_ref`/`*_refs` field; a unit test feeds each reader a `{slug, name}` Map
      and a plain id and gets the same answer.*
- [ ] **U2 — Wizard-level test per pack family.** One test per family
      (`toh`, `a5e-*`, `tob*`, `open5e`, …) that picks the pack as a source
      package and walks Identity → Class → Subclass → Proficiencies → Spells →
      Equipment → Feats, asserting each step renders options and the draft
      commits. This is the only gate that proves outcome 4; today
      `test/presentation/character_creation/` never loads a pack at all.
      *Exit: every bundled pack that ships a chargen category (class, subclass,
      species, subspecies, background, feat, spell) has a passing wizard test,
      and B1's `granted_at_level` change is asserted there (§5.2).*

### Stage B — fill the fields

- [ ] **B1 — Class/subclass level wiring.** Load `ClassFeatureItem.json`, group by
      `parent`, emit `features` rows (`level` + `name` + `description`) and
      `subclass.granted_at_level`.
      *Exit: `features` ≥ 95% on both categories, `granted_at_level` 100%, and
      `bundled_pack_resolve_test` shows a bundled subclass feature on the sheet.*
- [ ] **B2 — Class tables.** `feature_type == CORE_TRAITS_TABLE` + `column_value` →
      `cantrips_known_by_level` / `prepared_spells_by_level` / `spell_slots_by_level`
      / `extra_attack_count_by_level`.
- [ ] **B3 — Type-driven species/background mapping.** Match `SpeciesTrait.type` and
      `BackgroundBenefit.type` instead of names; add `tool_proficiency` and `feat`
      (both resolve to built-in cards — §2.3).
      *Exit: `size_ref`, `speed_ft`, `granted_skill_refs` at 100%.*
- [ ] **B4 — Spell gaps.** `shape_type`/`shape_size` → area fields;
      `reaction_condition` → `reaction_trigger`; load `SpellCastingOption.json` →
      `at_higher_levels_text`.
- [ ] **B5 — Grant block (§5.7).** Start with `mechanical_notes`: route every rule
      the mapper currently abandons in prose into it, one per line, so it reaches
      the sheet. Then the sourced keys. Also confirm/fix the
      `creature-action.damage_type_ref` regression and `monster.tags_line`.
- [ ] **B6 — Kill the gear stubs.** The 159 synthesised `adventuring-gear` entities
      carry no description, cost or weight, 47 of them are duplicates, and several
      are parse artifacts. Point background/class equipment refs at built-in gear
      by softRef and delete `_synthGearRef`; import `Item.json`/`Weapon.json`/
      `Armor.json` only for equipment a document genuinely introduces.
      *Exit: `adventuring-gear` count drops to only document-original items, and
      for **every** bundled background/class that ships `equipment_choice_groups`,
      `CharacterResolver` returns a non-empty `inventory` for each option — the
      check must be resolver-side, because `equipment_step._resolveItemLines`
      renders `ref['name']` even when the ref resolves to nothing, so a broken
      gear link looks perfect in the wizard and silently vanishes on the sheet.*
- [ ] **B7 — Close the policy rows.** Every `P`/`N`/⛔/⚪ row gets a one-line
      rationale **re-derived against §2.4**, so it stops reading as a bug. Decide
      what to do about the required-but-empty fields
      (`class.primary_ability_ref`, `background.origin_feat_ref`,
      `background.asi_distribution_options`, `spell.class_refs`): fill, or relax the
      requirement for third-party content.
- [ ] **B8 — Fix ToB3's action buckets.** 396 of `open5e-tob3`'s 397 monsters ship
      with an empty Actions block because their `CreatureAction.action_type` sends
      every row to bonus action / reaction / legendary (§3.5). Confirm the upstream
      values against the restored snapshot, then either correct the mapping or
      treat an implausible per-document distribution as an import error.
      *Exit: every pack's `action_refs` share is within range of the corpus, and
      no pack has more than a handful of monsters with zero actions.*

### Stage M — prove the mechanics land (outcome 2)

Fill percentage is not a mechanic working. These phases are what turn "the field
has a value" into "the value produced the right number on a sheet".

- [ ] **M1 — Extend `bundled_pack_resolve_test` to every pack.** *(no snapshot
      needed.)* Today it covers 3 of 19 assets with ~6 assertions, all about the
      three files `migrate_pack_assets.dart` rewrote. Make it data-driven: for each
      of the 19 assets, for each grant/typed mechanic key the asset actually
      writes, resolve one carrying entity through `CharacterResolver` and assert
      the effect appears (ability bonus applied, proficiency id present, sense
      listed, pool created, note rendered). The existing "no grant ref resolves to
      an empty string" sweep extends to all 19 for free.
      *Exit: for every (pack, mechanic field) pair present in the assets there is
      at least one passing sheet assertion, and the count is printed so a new
      field cannot land untested.*
- [ ] **M2 — `mechanical_notes` is measurable, not just written.** B5 routes
      abandoned prose into it; this phase proves it arrives. Add a per-category
      `mechanical_notes` fill line to the audit output, a resolver assertion that
      the note reaches `EffectiveCharacter.mechanicalNotes`, and a recorded
      **routing rate** (rules moved vs. rules the mapper still drops) so "the
      cheapest real win" has a number attached.
      *Exit: `mechanical_notes` non-zero on `feat` and `trait`, a sheet assertion
      per source card type, and a stated routing rate with the remainder logged to
      `unmapped_report.json`.*
- [ ] **M3 — Declare what stays non-mechanical.** `spell.effects` and
      `creature-action.effects` have a live editor but **no reader** in `domain/`
      or `application/`, and Open5e has no structured damage rows — so spell and
      action damage stays descriptive text under this audit. Write that down as a
      scope boundary instead of leaving it as an implicit 0%.
      *Exit: one paragraph in §5.6 and a line in "Done when"; no phase promises
      `effects`.*

### Stage T — prove the values are right (outcome 1)

- [ ] **T1 — `verify_packs.dart`: source ↔ asset differ.** `audit_packs.dart`
      counts values; nothing compares them to the fixtures. New tool: for each
      document, sample N entities per category, re-read their fixture rows and
      diff every mapped field, reporting *disagreements* (wrong value) separately
      from *absences* (unmapped). Run it over the full corpus for cheap fields and
      sampled for expensive ones.
      *Exit: V1 stops being manual — a green `verify_packs` run replaces
      "sampled against the fixtures", and every ⚠ constant is either confirmed
      correct against the source or filed as an `M`.*
- [ ] **T2 — Audit the built-in pack too.** *(no snapshot needed.)*
      `audit_packs.dart --builtin`: run the same declared-vs-filled census, the
      same ⚠-constant detection and the same undeclared-key footer over
      `generateBuiltinDnd5eV2Schema().seedRows` + `buildSrdCorePack()`. It is the
      target of every softRef this audit writes and it has never been measured.
      *Exit: a built-in census section added to §3; any hole that would make a
      planned softRef dangle (missing tool, gear, feat or spell name) is filed
      before the phase that would point at it. Fixes to it are a separate change
      with an `srdCorePackVersion` bump.*
- [ ] **T3 — Relational sanity gate.** *(no snapshot needed.)* Per-entity
      completeness checks the field census structurally cannot express, run over
      the assets and failing the build: every `monster` has ≥1 action; no
      `creature-action` / `trait` row is orphaned; every `subclass` resolves its
      `parent_class_ref`; every `equipment_choice_groups` option resolves at least
      one item; per-pack bucket distributions (`action_refs` vs bonus / reaction /
      legendary) stay inside a corpus-wide band. §3.5 exists because none of these
      were checked and `open5e-tob3` shipped 396 actionless statblocks.
      *Exit: the checks run in CI over `assets/open5e_packs/` and are green, or
      each exception is recorded with a reason.*

### Stage V — verify what already ships

- [ ] **V1 — Re-verify every green row.** The from-scratch requirement in §0:
      each ✅ and ✅⚠ row in §5 is checked against the source once, not assumed.
      Start with the known ⚠ constants (`creature_type_ref`, `repeatable`,
      `is_cursed`, `is_sentient`, `activation`, `trait_kind`, gear `cost_cp` /
      `weight_lb`) — each is a mapper default masquerading as coverage. **Driven by
      T1**; hand-sampling 125 filled (category, field) slots across 20,712 entities
      is not a repeatable gate.
      *Exit: no ⚠ marker left without a recorded "this default is correct"
      rationale, and `verify_packs` covers every ✅ row.*

### Stage D — deliver it (nothing above reaches a user without this)

- [ ] **D1 — Version and publish.** Decide and implement the versioning rule:
      `emit.dart` must stop hardcoding `pack_version: '1.0.0'` (derive it from the
      source rev + a content hash, or bump it explicitly per release), because
      `r2_path` is `package/<slug>@<version>.json.gz` and `publish_catalog` skips
      an object that already exists. Then rebuild the catalog and publish.
      *Exit: `build_catalog.dart` → `publish_catalog.dart --dry-run` reports every
      changed pack as an **upload**, not a skip; `requires`, `counts` and
      `size_bytes` are current (§3.3 drift cleared); no `--force` needed.*
- [ ] **D2 — Upgrade and uninstall paths.** Two holes L1/L2 open:
      (a) an already-installed pack has no upgrade trigger — `FirstPartyInstallNotifier`
      never compares the stored `metadata.catalog_version` against the manifest, so
      a user who installed `@1.0.0` keeps the duplicated, empty-field version
      forever; (b) once one pack owns content others link, uninstalling the owner
      silently strips content from the linkers — `PackageLinkService.reverseLinks`
      exists for exactly this warning but is not wired into the official-pack
      uninstall path.
      *Exit: the Packages tab offers an update when a newer catalog version
      exists, and uninstalling a linked-to official pack warns with the list of
      packs that link it.*
      *Also decide and record:* what happens to a character or world that
      references an entity L1/L2 deleted. Ids are uuidv5 and stable, so a dropped
      entity is a dangling ref in existing data — the soft-ref rule makes it a
      warning rather than a crash, but "the monster lost half its actions" is a
      user-visible regression that needs a stated policy.

### Done when

All four outcomes in §0.1 are demonstrable, not just ticked:

1. **Content** — every row in §5 is ✅, ⛔ or ⚪ (no 🔴/🟡 without a cause code
   that says it cannot be fixed), measured by `audit_packs.dart`'s full output
   (**407 declared (category, field) slots, 125 filled today**) rather than by the
   abridged tables in §5; `verify_packs` (T1) is green; the built-in pack has been
   measured once (T2); and the relational gate (T3) passes — no monster without
   actions, no orphaned child row, every `parent_class_ref` resolving.
2. **Mechanics** — every (pack, mechanic field) pair has a sheet assertion (M1),
   `mechanical_notes` has a stated routing rate (M2), and what stays
   non-mechanical is written down (M3).
3. **Linking** — `dupe_census.dart` (post-L0) reports no redundancy a recorded
   policy does not explain, section C's "nothing installed" is 0 under
   runtime-identical matching, and every linker ships both link keys plus a
   non-empty `requires`.
4. **Character creation** — a wizard test per pack family passes (U2), and no
   chargen filter reads a `*_ref` field as a raw id (U1).
5. **Delivery** — a published catalog whose packs upload rather than skip (D1),
   with an upgrade path for existing installs (D2).

In app terms: installing a third-party pack and picking one of its subclasses
produces a character sheet with that subclass's features on it; the user's pickers
show each piece of content exactly once; and the pack the user downloads today is
the pack this audit fixed. At that point this file becomes a record, and
`open5e_import_roadmap.md` goes back to being the primary doc.

**Planned tools** (do not exist yet — the phase that adds them owns the command):
`audit_packs.dart --builtin` (T2), `verify_packs.dart` (T1), and the
`dupe_census.dart` fidelity flags of L0.

**The §2.5 text-divergence measurement**, until L0 folds it into the census. Run
from `flutter_app/`; it is the number §2.5 and §3.2 quote:

```sh
python3 - <<'PY'
import json,glob,collections,hashlib
rows=collections.defaultdict(list)
for f in glob.glob('assets/open5e_packs/*.pkg.json'):
    for v in json.load(open(f))['entities'].values():
        if v.get('type') in ('creature-action','trait'):
            d=((v.get('attributes') or {}).get('description') or '').strip()
            rows[(v['type'],v['name'].strip().lower())].append(hashlib.md5(d.encode()).hexdigest())
multi=[v for v in rows.values() if len(v)>1]
diff=[v for v in multi if len(set(v))>1]
print(f'shared names {len(multi)}, differing text {len(diff)} ({100*len(diff)/len(multi):.1f}%)')
PY
```

`bundled_pack_resolve_test.dart` is the right place to prove a B- or L-phase
landed: it walks an asset the way an install does — resolve every `{_lookup, name}`
against the campaign's Tier-0 rows, then hand the entity to `CharacterResolver` —
so it catches the case where a field is written but nothing reads it, and the case
where a ref points at a card that no longer ships.

**Drift-backed tests on Linux:** `package:sqlite3` opens `libsqlite3.so`, which only
exists with `libsqlite3-dev` installed. `test/support/test_database.dart`
(`openTestDatabase()`) registers a resolver falling back to `libsqlite3.so.0`, so
use it rather than `NativeDatabase.memory()` directly. `v12_schema_smoke_test.dart`
is not on the helper yet and still fails with "Failed to load dynamic library" on
such hosts — that failure is environmental, not a regression.

A full `flutter test` run also has a sizable pre-existing failing set (~61 tests on
a clean tree). Diff against a clean-HEAD worktree before attributing any failure to
this work.
